newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline shares jump on Roche talk.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline shares jump on Roche talk.

text.p: Shares in Anglo-U.S. drugs group SmithKline Beecham Plc jumped in late trading on Wednesday on rumours that Swiss drugs giant Roche Holdings AG may be preparing for a hostile bid or agreed merger.
Traders said rumours that Roche has been trying to put together a funding package of up to 50 billion Swiss francs had sparked the speculation.
SmithKline share closed up 30-1/2 pence at 810.
A SmithKline Beecham spokesman said the company "never comments on market rumours."

Traders said rumours that Roche had been trying to put together a sizeable credit line have been circulating for a few days. The company has previously been touted as a possible suitor for another British company, Zeneca Group Plc.

SmithKline had a market capitalization of around 21.3 billion stg at the close of trading on Wednesday. Roche, which is worth around 95.1 billion Swiss francs, already has a cash pile of around six billion Swiss francs to fund any ambitions it might have.
Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull's director of equity research Paul Diggle said "don't hold your breath, but it isn't that stupid."

Diggle said, however, that a merger between the two companies was more feasible than a hostile takeover. He noted that both Roche and SmithKline have made no secret of their desire to be bigger, and a merger could "satisfy the ambition of both companies."
A merger would give Roche and SmithKline Beecham a combined world market share of more than five percent, putting them on a par with the current world leader Glaxo Wellcome Plc.
SmithKline would also offer Roche a much firmer footing in the key U.S. market, where is lacks critical mass.
Roche's vitamin business, which is the biggest in the world, would provide a useful fit with SmithKline' consumer healthcare and over-the-counter drugs operations.
Both companies have strong portfolios of central nervous sytem drugs and antibiotics.
